costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an N16B16A typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: (A used N16B16A engine is available from approximately £1,295 supply-only. A replacement motor averages £2,625 in good condition, with reconditioned units up to £3,632. All figures . Fitted = supply price + labour band below.)

What moves the price for the N16B16A is whether the timing chain, guides and tensioner have been replaced (the primary failure on these engines), whether the Valvetronic system has been serviced, and whether the engine comes complete with ancillaries (alternator, starter, injectors) or as a bare long block. A used engine with documented timing chain history commands a premium; a bare block with ancillaries removed is cheaper. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide.

failures.title: MINI N16B16A Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing chain guide wear and tensioner failure - all years
items.whatHappens: The timing chain and tensioner on the N16 are known for a modest service life - sometimes less than 100,000 km. The plastic guides become brittle over time, and as the tensioner spring weakens, the chain can slacken, causing a characteristic ticking or rattling noise. If the chain skips, pistons can contact valves, causing catastrophic internal engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early - when the rattle first appears - replacing the timing chain kit (chain, guides, tensioner) is the cost-effective fix. Chain replacement typically costs £800-£1,500 at an independent specialist. If ignored and the chain jumps, the engine will typically need a full replacement or rebuild.

items.title: Valvetronic and VANOS system wear - all years
items.whatHappens: The Valvetronic system (variable valve lift) and VANOS phase regulators are known weak points on the N16. Wear in these systems can cause rough idling, hesitation on acceleration, reduced power, and engine management lights.
items.repairVsReplace: Valvetronic motor or eccentric shaft issues can be significant - £600-£1,200. VANOS solenoid cleaning or replacement typically costs £300-£600.

items.title: Oil consumption and intake coking - higher-mileage units
items.whatHappens: Many Prince-family engines - including the N16 - develop oil consumption issues as they age, often due to worn piston rings or valve stem seals. Intake valve coking (carbon deposits) is also common due to the direct injection design.
items.repairVsReplace: If consumption is mild (1L per 1,000 miles), regular top-ups may be tolerable. Severe consumption (1L per 500 miles or less) typically requires engine strip-down - often uneconomical versus fitting a replacement unit. Carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) costs £400-£700.

items.title: Thermostat and water pump failure - all years
items.whatHappens: The thermostat and water pump are weak points on this engine family. Failure leads to coolant leaks, incorrect engine temperature, and can trigger the engine management light.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacement of the thermostat and water pump typically costs £400-£800. Ignoring it risks overheating and head gasket damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: The N16B16A is considered more reliable than its predecessor, the N12. While it shares many of the Prince family's weaknesses, the naturally aspirated design is simpler and less stressed than the turbocharged N14 and N18 variants. Post-2010 engines received running improvements to the timing chain tensioner and Valvetronic components.

variants.title: N16B16A - One Engine, Multiple Tunes
variants.intro: The N16B16A is a specific engine code within BMW's Prince engine family, but it spans multiple power outputs and vehicle applications. The core hardware - 1.6-litre aluminium block, 77mm bore × 85.8mm stroke, 11.0:1 compression ratio - is consistent across all variants; tuning differentiates them. Fitted to: MINI Cooper (R56/R55/R57/R58/R59/R60/R61) - all body styles Key technical difference: 90 kW (122 PS) at 6,000 rpm, 160 Nm torque at 4,250 rpm. This is the most common N16B16A variant fitted to UK MINIs. Features double VANOS and Valvetronic. Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above (timing chain guide wear, Valvetronic/VANOS wear, oil consumption, thermostat/water pump failure). Interchange note: Direct swap with other N16B16A Cooper variants of the same year. The 122 hp Cooper unit can be fitted to a One with the correct ECU calibration. Fitted to: MINI One (R56/R55/R57) Key technical difference: Lower output - 55-72 kW (75-98 PS), 140-153 Nm torque. Same hardware, different ECU calibration. Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family pattern; lower power output means marginally less stress on timing components.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement N16B16A - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used N16B16A makes sense for lower-value R-series MINIs where a reconditioned unit would exceed the car's value. However, the timing chain is the critical risk - only buy a used unit with documented chain history or from a car that was running well at removal. Mileage under 60,000 is preferable. A used bare engine can be found from approximately £1,295.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the sweet spot for most N16B16A replacements. A proper reconditioned unit will have the timing chain, guides and tensioner replaced (addressing the primary failure), new Valvetronic components, new piston rings (addressing oil consumption), and a carbon-cleaned cylinder head. Expect 12-24 months warranty and a price of £1,600-£2,400. A reconditioned engine can cost up to £3,632.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is necessary if the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure (valve-piston contact) or severe oil consumption that has damaged cylinder bores. A rebuilt engine should include new pistons, rings, bearings, timing components, a rebuilt cylinder head, and new Valvetronic components. Expect £2,400-£3,600 supply-only.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: EnginesMarket connects you with vetted UK MINI specialists who can supply and fit your N16B16A - nationwide delivery and a minimum 12-month warranty on all reconditioned units.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The N16B16A sits in R-series MINIs typically valued between £1,500 (early One high-mileage) and £8,000 (low-mileage Cooper). If your MINI is worth less than £3,000, a reconditioned unit at £1,600-£2,400 represents 50-80% of the car's value - carefully evaluate whether replacement makes financial sense. For lower-value examples, a good used engine with documented history may be the better economic choice. If the car is worth under £2,000, evaluate scrap value before committing to a reconditioned engine.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the N16B16A engine?
items.answer: Timing chain guide wear and tensioner failure is the primary concern, typically appearing between 60,000-100,000 km (37,000-62,000 miles). A ticking or rattling noise is the earliest warning. If caught early, a chain kit replacement (£800-£1,500) prevents catastrophic failure; if ignored, the chain can jump and destroy the engine. Valvetronic and VANOS system wear causes rough idling and hesitation (£300-£1,200). Oil consumption and intake valve coking on higher-mileage units (80,000+ miles) are also common. Thermostat and water pump failure (£400-£800) is another known weakness.

items.question: Is the N16B16A a reliable engine overall?
items.answer: The N16B16A is considered more reliable than its predecessor, the N12, and significantly less complex than its turbocharged siblings (N14, N18). With proper maintenance - including 5W-30 LL-01 oil, regular coolant checks, and 10,000-mile service intervals - the N16 can be a dependable entry-level engine. The naturally aspirated design is simpler and less stressed than turbocharged variants. Timing chain guide wear remains the primary weakness - listen for rattling noises. Regular oil changes with BMW-approved oil are essential to prevent timing chain and Valvetronic issues. Post-2010 engines have revised timing chain tensioner components that have improved reliability.
